purpose: Configuration benchmarks for the controls that cite neither CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations nor CISA ScubaGear in controls.json. relations.Equivalent: Same setting and threshold: the control passes exactly when the item passes.
relations.Subset: The control checks part of what the item requires; the rest is named in Unchecked.
relations.Stricter: The control passes only when the item passes, and can fail where the item passes.

AAD-1.2.ItemTitle: Microsoft Entra ID must be configured to use multifactor authentication (MFA).
AAD-1.2.Why: The check verifies a Conditional Access MFA policy whose state is On with 'All users' included and any user exclusions documented with the AO; the fix grants 'Require multifactor authentication' on All cloud apps. Satisfied requires an enabled policy including All users on All cloud apps that requires MFA (or an authentication strength, which requires MFA), with no exclusions or only exclusions on the tenant's approval record, and is stricter on apps, client types and registration.
AAD-1.2.Unchecked: Whether the exclusion approval is documented with the authorizing official: the tool's EmergencyAccess record names an approver and dates but cannot establish that the approver is the AO, so an approved exclusion passes here and still needs the AO documentation the STIG check asks for.

AAD-11.3.ItemId: All risky workload identities are triaged (Zero Trust Assessment test 21862)
AAD-11.3.ItemTitle: All risky workload identities are triaged
AAD-11.3.Why: Microsoft's check fails when identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals returns any service principal with riskState 'atRisk' (or any servicePrincipalRiskDetection is atRisk). The evaluator reads the same collection and is Satisfied only when none is atRisk (it also fails on confirmedCompromised, which the check does not), so Satisfied passes that half of the check.
AAD-11.3.Unchecked: The check's second half, identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections with riskState 'atRisk', is not read; an untriaged detection on a principal whose aggregate state is not atRisk would fail the check and pass here.

AAD-14.1.ItemId: Application certificates must be rotated on a regular basis (Zero Trust Assessment test 21992)
AAD-14.1.ItemTitle: Application certificates must be rotated on a regular basis
AAD-14.1.Why: Microsoft: 'Query all of your service principals and application registrations that have certificate credentials. Make sure the certificate start date is less than 180 days' (test 21992 fails on a keyCredential whose startDateTime is more than 180 days ago). For app registrations, Satisfied requires every certificate to be unexpired with more than 30 days left and a lifetime of 180 days or less, so its start date is less than 150 days ago and the app-registration half of the check passes.
AAD-14.1.Unchecked: Certificate credentials on service principals (the check queries both applications and servicePrincipals keyCredentials); the collector reads /applications only.

AAD-3.4.ItemId: Step 6: Configure PIM > Configure activation settings > 'Require justification'
AAD-3.4.ItemTitle: For each privileged role ... Configure settings: Require justification
AAD-3.4.Why: The guide's step sets 'Require justification' on the PIM activation settings of each privileged role, which is the Justification entry in the role policy's Enablement_EndUser_Assignment rule the evaluator reads; Satisfied means every policy for the 17 roles the tool treats as privileged (which include Microsoft's stated minimum set: Global, Privileged Role, Security, Exchange and SharePoint Administrator) has it.
AAD-3.4.Unchecked: Roles the organization identifies as privileged beyond the tool's fixed 17-role list (for example Hybrid Identity Administrator or custom roles) are not judged when the policy-to-role map is available. The other settings in the same step (require MFA, maximum duration, approval) are separate controls (AAD-3.3, AAD-3.6, AAD-3.5).

DNS-1.4.ItemTitle: Receiving domains should implement protocols to signal TLS usage to clients. Receivers should implement DANE, MTA-STS (or both) for all mail servers listed in the domain's MX Resource Record set.
DNS-1.4.Why: A published MTA-STS record with a retrievable policy in enforce mode is MTA-STS implemented for the domain; enforce is the mode in which, per Section 5.2.5 Table 5-2, a client rejects the connection on a TLS validation or MX matching failure. The policy's mx: patterns must also cover every host in the domain's MX RR set (RFC 8461 wildcard matching), the recommendation's 'for all mail servers listed' part.
DNS-1.4.Unchecked: That each MX host presents a certificate matching the policy; max_age; domains not in the assessed DNS domain list. (DANE alone also passes the recommendation, where DNS-1.4 would report a Gap.)

DNS-1.6.ItemTitle: Organizations should deploy DNSSEC for all DNS name servers and validate DNSSEC responses from all systems that receive email.
DNS-1.6.Why: A DS record at the parent (or a signed enclosing zone) shows the domain's zone is DNSSEC-signed and delegated securely, which is the deploy-DNSSEC half of the recommendation for that domain.
DNS-1.6.Unchecked: DNSSEC validation by the organization's receiving mail systems (Exchange Online's validation is Microsoft's); that the signatures actually validate (a DS with broken signatures still passes); domains not in the assessed list.

DNS-2.1.Why: Satisfied requires a key of at least 2048 bits rotated within 365 days, inside the row's recommended length and its 1-2 year lifetime. When the key size could not be read, the rotation verdict stands and the Detail says the size was not judged.

AAD-10.4.Reason: The evaluator accepts any enabled policy with any interval and any scope. Near-misses that fail the rule: Zero Trust Assessment checks 'Privileged users have short-lived sign-in sessions' (test 21825: every privileged role covered by an enabled policy with sign-in frequency 4 hours or less) and 'Guests don't have long lived sign-in sessions' (test 21824: a policy targeting guests or external users at 24 hours or less, 1 day, or every time) - a 30-day frequency on one group is Satisfied here and fails both. DISA STIG V-270200 (session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity) is a different setting (idle session timeout), not sign-in frequency. ScubaGear 2.0.0 has no sign-in frequency rule.
AAD-10.4.EarnBy: Add a per-population judgment: for each privileged role, an enabled policy including that role with signInFrequency type hours and value 4 or less (cite ZTA 21825), and for guests an enabled policy with includeGuestsOrExternalUsers and 24 hours or less (cite ZTA 21824). The collector would need to store signInFrequency.type and .value.

AAD-11.5.Reason: No configuration benchmark recommends CAE strict enforcement as a value. ScubaGear 2.0.0 and the DISA Entra ID STIG V1R1 have no CAE rule; the Learn 'Configure Microsoft Entra for increased security' checks have only 'Network validation is configured through Universal Continuous Access Evaluation', a Global Secure Access feature (Entra Internet/Private Access) that is a different setting. Microsoft's CAE documentation describes strict location enforcement as an option, not a recommended baseline value.

AAD-11.6.Reason: ScubaGear 2.0.0 section 8 covers guest access, invitations and allowed domains, not inbound trust; the DISA Entra ID STIG V1R1 has no cross-tenant rule; the Zero Trust checks include only 'Outbound cross-tenant access settings are configured' (outbound B2B collaboration blocked by default), a different setting, and 'Guest access is protected by strong authentication methods', which suggests accepting the MFA claim for vetted partners rather than recommending it off. No benchmark states the default inbound-trust value the evaluator requires.

AAD-11.8.Reason: ScubaGear 2.0.0 and the Zero Trust checks have no Terms of Use item. Near-miss: DISA STIG V-270209 (ENTR-ID-000150) requires the DOD Notice and Consent banner in the company branding sign-in page text, a different setting (organizational branding signInPageText), not a CA Terms of Use grant; a tenant with a ToU policy and no banner passes here and fails the STIG.
AAD-11.8.EarnBy: Not this control: V-270209 would need a separate check of /organization/{id}/branding signInPageText for the banner text (DoD tenants only).

AAD-12.3.Reason: Near-miss: DISA STIG V-270204 (ENTR-ID-000090) audits enabled users whose last sign-in is older than 35 days (or never signed in and created more than 35 days ago). The evaluator's 90-day threshold is looser and it ignores unlicensed members, so an account idle for 60 days is Satisfied here and a finding under the STIG. The Zero Trust checks cover inactive guests and stale privileged identities, not all members; ScubaGear 2.0.0 has no inactive-account rule.
AAD-12.3.EarnBy: A STIG-mode threshold of 35 days over all enabled members (licensed or not) would earn V-270204 as Subset (guests would still be AAD-12.2's); keep the 90-day verdict for non-DoD tenants.

AAD-13.1.Reason: Secure Score is Microsoft's own scoring of many settings, not a configuration setting, and no benchmark sets a Secure Score threshold. AAD-3.6.Reason: No benchmark states a firm maximum PIM activation duration that 8 hours meets. ScubaGear 2.0.0 and the DISA Entra ID STIG V1R1 have no activation-duration rule, and the Zero Trust Assessment checks have none. Near-misses: Zero Trust Phase 1 Step 6 says 'Set maximum activation duration (for example: 1-4 hours for high-impact roles)', an example, and looser than the evaluator's 8-hour threshold would need to be to pass it (a 6-hour setting is Satisfied here and outside 1-4 hours); the PIM deployment plan shows 'example settings' (Global Administrator one hour, Exchange Admin two hours). Neither is a stated recommended value the 8-hour Satisfied state always meets.
AAD-3.6.EarnBy: Not a small change: Microsoft gives only examples. If the owner adopts the Zero Trust 1-4 hour range as the requirement for the high-impact roles, tighten the threshold to 4 hours for those roles and cite Zero Trust Phase 1 Step 6 as Subset; note the collector's 'PT(\d+)H' parse returns null for minute-only durations such as PT30M, which the evaluator then reports as not assessed.

AAD-8.2.Reason: ScubaGear 2.0.0 has no access-review rule; the DISA Entra ID STIG V1R1 has none; the Learn 'Configure Microsoft Entra for increased security' checks have none for role reviews. The Zero Trust Assessment repository has a test 21855 'Privileged roles have access reviews' but it is unimplemented ('Planned for future release', skipped as UnderConstruction) and is not published on the Learn page, so it has no audit to match. The ID Governance deployment guide says 'Create access reviews for Global Administrators' without a configuration value, and the evaluator would pass on a review of any single role, not necessarily Global Administrator.
AAD-8.2.EarnBy: If Microsoft publishes 21855 with criteria, read each review's scope (role definition ids) and recurrence (settings.recurrence) and require that every privileged role, at minimum Global Administrator, is covered by a recurring review.
